title: Kobi <> Taryn: Daily Sync

items.topic: Testing next week, UAT not imminent
items.statement: Kobi reported that after the day's client call the team is not rushing into UAT; next week's session is testing, which he described as UAT-like but more testing.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, okay. It was an interesting call today. Um, looks like we're slowing down a little bit in terms of um, pace. I mean, adding adding a whole bunch of stuff to what we're going to deliver, but uh, we're not necessarily rushing to go into UAT anytime soon, which is kind of good. Well, I guess like next week's testing is kind of UAT, but it's more testing.

items.topic: Delivery scope growing after client call
items.statement: Kobi said a lot of additional items are being added to what Jumpr will deliver.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... adding adding a whole bunch of stuff to what we're going to deliver

items.feature_area: Other (ID mapping; area not stated in this doc)
items.topic: ID mapping confusion in client call
items.statement: Taryn noted there was some confusion in the day's client call about the ID mapping part and felt there was miscommunication on it.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: Um I feel like like other than the small confusion with um what was it the ID mapping part of it? Um, I feel like it was um, pretty good. / Taryn Reithofer: ... because there's a lot of at least with that it sounded like there was a lot of miscommunication.

items.topic: Client asks diverge from PRD
items.statement: Kobi said Jumpr receives different information from different client stakeholders and the current asks do not match the requirements in the client PRD that the design was based on, so changes are being made.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we get different different information from different people and then their all the requirements that they gave us in their PRD doesn't necessarily match what they're asking for now. So we've designed based on that and then now we're going in and change making changes which again it's fine.

items.topic: Rep UI first, ops UI later
items.statement: Kobi suggested focusing on one UI at a time: settle the clean, simple rep UI first, then work through an ops-focused UI where showing many fields is acceptable because ops use it less often (for example when configuring deals).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... Um, and it's sometimes it's helpful just focus on one UI first. Let's get that hashed out and then we'll have the the op focus UI that we can work through because for them it shouldn't be a problem seeing all those fields. / Kobi Kunasekaran: They go in maybe when they're configuring deals and stuff.
items.note: Internal Jumpr view; not confirmed with client in this doc.

items.topic: Prefer sprints with shippable chunks
items.statement: Kobi said he would rather work in sprints that ship a chunk of features, get feedback, and iterate.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: let's work in like uh in sprints to ship out like uh like a good chunk of features um and get feedback and like keep going that way.
items.note: Internal preference only; no client agreement in this doc.

items.topic: November 1 overall target
items.statement: Kobi said the client gave an overall target of November 1 for everything, and that nothing would be live for roughly another two months.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... it does mean, you know, like we're going to keep working at this and not really going to see an see something out there until for like another like two months / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... like they gave us a they gave us a like overall target goab November 1st for everything.

items.topic: Original sign-up logging MVP phase abandoned
items.statement: Kobi said the original phasing was to go live first with the sign-up logging experience (agency website clicks into Salesforce, reps use buttons, sign-up and player records created automatically), with other workflows added one by one, targeting go-live around next week; the project has since moved away from that approach. Taryn noted the client pushed back its timeline.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: That was that was the initial intention right the initially what we talked about and we kind of like phased out / Kobi Kunasekaran: the project is we'll do the signup logging experience so their website the agency website the the clicks will come into Salesforce and then reps will go in um they have the buttons they have the uh signup records created the player record created um all of that will be automated / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... So the goal was by like next week we would be live with that whole signup blogging / Kobi Kunasekaran: experience. So we'll have reps in Salesforce and then we work in you know increments for everything else. But now we kind of stayed away from that quite a bit. / Taryn Reithofer: ... I'm appreciative that they've pushed back their timeline
items.supersedes_hint: Earlier plan: sign-up logging MVP live around the week of 2026-08-17, other pieces incremental; now moved away from that, overall target November 1.

items.topic: Spreadsheets run in parallel until validated
items.statement: Kobi recalled the earlier plan that reps would keep recording some data in their spreadsheets until the team validated everything, after which the spreadsheets would be deprecated.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... And we talked about like them still recording some of that stuff in their spreadsheets just to make sure that until we're up to speed and we validated everything and then we deprecate the spreadsheets.
items.note: Recollection of an earlier plan; current status not stated.

items.topic: Agency website sign-up click testing
items.statement: Kobi said one of his questions in the client call was about testing the agency website bringing sign-up clicks in, and that the test plan walkthrough covered it.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um were you there when they talked through the test plan? / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... So like my questions were around um the testing for the agency website like bringing those signup clicks in.

items.topic: CMS integration still in progress, no target
items.statement: The client's update on the CMS integration was that they are still working through it; no specific target was given beyond the overall November 1 goal.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... and the second one for the CMS integration. It like they're still working through it. So that was their update, / Taryn Reithofer: So, no target go / Kobi Kunasekaran: There was nothing.

items.topic: Start discovery on other components
items.statement: Kobi suggested breaking the work up and starting discovery for other components over the next few weeks so Jumpr has work while the client resolves CMS.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... Um, but I think we need to start like breaking this up and start doing discovery for the other other components uh over the next few weeks so that we can we have stuff to work on while their CMS stuff works out and everything else, right?

items.topic: Two new users get same access as client ops managers
items.statement: Two new client users are to be set up with the same access as Joyce, Emily and Lena (ops managers, matching Joyce's setup) rather than the sales rep role, because they are working on the integration. Kobi said the ticket was updated to reflect this.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: ... in terms of adding these two reps, um, there's just one contradiction. So, in the to-do, you say, um, both reps have the same access as Joyce, Emily, and Lena. But then um Jester is asking me to add them as sales reps as a role within Salesforce. / Kobi Kunasekaran: you can let them know. I don't know you saw the updated ticket. Um, but basically I assume that because they're working on the integration, um, I figured it'll make more sense for them to have like all of the access similar to what everybody else does as opposed to just reps. / Kobi Kunasekaran: They're going to be I I I would say set them up exactly how Joyce uh Joyce is set up.
items.asr_note: Jester = Chester [ASR?]; Lena vs 'Lita' in Gemini notes [ASR?]

items.topic: Org access is permission-set driven
items.statement: Kobi said WagerTech is being set up to be permission-set driven, using permission sets and permission set groups so new features can be tied to a permission set without updating profiles.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... we're setting up wager tags to be permission set driven. / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... we try to do everything around permission sets and permission set groups so that if we need to deploy a new feature we can just tie to that permission set. / Kobi Kunasekaran: We don't have to go and update profiles and mess with all of that.

items.topic: Maintain user-facing training manual
items.statement: Keep the sign-up logging training material as one living, user-facing document that is updated as feedback arrives and processes change; it can be handed to the client (for example Emily) to train new reps. There is no hard deliverable date.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... So let's like let's keep that as one one document that we're going to like keep building on to um as you know as we work through the process as things / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... obviously like there's no hard deliverable date for that right now. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So we can just hand them over to Emily for example if she wants to train new reps we can use that uh to train reps and even give it to them as reference later.

items.topic: Rep sign-up list process and buttons
items.statement: Kobi described the defined rep process: reps go to the sign-up list, click into it, and work through buttons he described as four, naming new, in progress and archived. He said client feedback is expected Thursday or Friday.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... since they're they told us you know they're going to come back with more feedback and stuff uh Thursday Friday. / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... Like we know they're going to go into the the signup list. They're going to click on the list. They're going to they have the four buttons to work through uh either new in progress archived.
items.note: Only three of the 'four buttons' are named in the transcript.

items.statement: Kobi asked Taryn to start an admin user manual, beginning with user management and covering which permission sets exist, what each does and when to add each; user stories should carry a note to update the documentation.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... Um and then on the flip side I think I don't think we have a admin documentation yet. / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... let's start building uh admin user manual / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... Uh, the first thing is going to be user management, right? / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... we'll just need to make sure that as we create those user stories that we have a note to go in and update the documentation too. / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... So, what I actually wanted to be covered in the documentation is like what are the permission sets, what do each do, and when to add each one.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: UAT request submission process defined The project team will require the client to use formal Asana form submissions for requests once the project enters the UAT phase to improve tracking and reduce friction.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Taryn Reithofer: most. It's almost as if they need to use a form submission in a sauna, but I don't know if that's unfair for us to ask based on how informal this has been because that's pretty / Kobi Kunasekaran: Like that's a challenge where like I accept something like this at this stage because adding that level of it basically adds friction to them. / Kobi Kunasekaran: something like that I think is absolutely necessary the moment we go into UAT.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary lists this as an aligned decision that the client will be required to use Asana forms. Transcript shows only an internal suggestion by Taryn and Kobi's view that something like it is necessary at UAT; no decision or client agreement, and Kobi said it adds friction (summary says it reduces friction).

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Project momentum concerns persist due to client communication difficulties and internal misalignment. The team identified that adopting an incremental delivery model is necessary to avoid further delays.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: let's work in like uh in sprints to ship out like uh like a good chunk of features um and get feedback and like keep going that way.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary presents incremental delivery as a team finding that is necessary; transcript shows Kobi's personal preference only, with no agreed change to the delivery approach.

notes: Internal Jumpr 1:1 following a WagerTech client call the same day. Only WagerTech delivery/scope passages extracted. Status and plan statements are Jumpr-internal views; no client party was present, so no item is a client-confirmed decision. Action items are internal assignments between Kobi and Taryn.
